ncu_status.model_process_ncu: NOT_RUN (no kernel profiled). Attempt 1 (session 2, 18:30-18:46Z, ncu16k, --set full): startup under ncu exceeded the 32G cgroup MemoryHigh (34.4 GiB, pressure 85%); /health polls timed out and the API guard latched 'Protocol cleanup failed' (sticky 503); aborted at the parent's cap. Attempt 2 (session 3, 19:59-20:13Z, ncu120k-b, 5 sections, MemoryHigh 42G/MemoryMax 44G): ready after 146 s with memory.peak 38.9 GiB, then the 120K layer-major prefill grew host memory to the 44G cap (thrash, ~layer 2 after 3.5 min, first kernel replay never completed); ended; the 16K follow-up could not start before the session ended (transient unit still loaded).
ncu_status.root_cause: ncu kernel-replay injection adds ~11 GiB host memory at startup (38.9 vs 27.7 GiB peak under nsys) and grows further during the expert-streaming prefill; on this 48 GiB WSL host a model-process ncu run cannot fit the experiment unit memory envelope.

evidence.observation: 8 CTAs x 1 warp move ~30-33 GB/s (ncu) while the copy engine reaches ~34-41 GB/s on the same link; the gather sits serially on the decode critical chain (single-stream graph).

estimate.assumption: hide 50% of gather time (more TMA requests in flight to reach copy-engine bandwidth, plus issuing layer L+1's likely misses during layer L on a side stream); transport only -> bit-exact

ranked_top3.name: Fresh-prompt expert streaming: every fresh prefill copies the whole 18.25 GB NVFP4 expert bank over PCIe

estimate.assumption: skip experts already resident in decode slots (~31% of the bank, 3164 of 40x256) on fresh prefills; same bytes for the rest -> bit-exact
estimate.note: the single-chunk (short prompt) path overlaps only ~12% of the copy with compute; even a perfect overlap cannot go below ~(1-resident)*18.25 GB / 40 GB/s ~ 0.32 s for a fresh short prompt

ranked_top3.name: Decode weight-streaming kernels below the DRAM roofline: MoE NVFP4 marlin (~59% of 896 GB/s) and the out/o-projection still on cuBLAS FP8 xmma + split-K reduce

evidence.note: marlin/xmma were not profiled with ncu (NOT_RUN); marlin efficiency is bytes/time from the nsys trace

estimate.assumption: bit-exact GEMV-style kernels at ~85% of DRAM peak for the 8 routed experts, and the existing QMMA FP8 GEMV (2048x4096 measured) replacing xmma + split-K (needs a bit-exact replica of cuBLAS split-K=3 order)

other_candidates.name: 120K prefill attention (65% of 120K TTFT)
other_candidates.estimate: prefill is tensor-pipe bound (SM ~82%, HMMA ~44.5% of instruction peak = pipe ~90% busy; top stall math_pipe_throttle); decode attention already at ~94% of DRAM peak. Bit-exact headroom <= ~5-10% (k=4 grouping, wave tail) ~ -0.7..-1.4 s at 120K; larger gains need non-bit-exact FP8 attention.

other_candidates.name: Prefill MoE expert GEMM (CUDA NVFP4 fast_gemm, 36% of 16K / 17% of 120K prefill)
other_candidates.estimate: compute-bound on the BF16 HMMA pipe (SM ~83%) because bit-exactness pins the Triton BF16 dequant+HMMA order; headroom ~10% (-50 ms at 16K, -0.36 s at 120K) unless an FP4/FP8 MMA path is accepted with a new quality gate.

other_candidates.name: Decode launch bubbles (~998 graph nodes per step)
other_candidates.estimate: fusing router/top-k/LRU/sum-reduce and norm+quant chains (or PDL) ~ -0.2..-0.3 ms/step (+3-4%)

levers.note: Estimates derive from profiler-time shares (nsys) and component ncu; confirm with unprofiled paired A/B.

notes: All timings were taken under Nsight (Systems or Compute) and are diagnostic only; speed acceptance needs unprofiled paired runs.

Critical path = analyze-model-nsys.py latest-finishing-predecessor chain per forward (overlapped work is not summed); decode = sum of step periods with the last step of each request excluded; prefill = whole layer-major window (under layer-major the entire prefill is ONE forward).
cpu_gaps_gpu_idle = GPU idle inside forwards + between forwards on the critical chain (host launch/sync/scheduler).
gpu.busy_pct/idle_bubble_pct = union of all traced GPU ops in the scenario window (kernels+copies+memsets).

kernels[] are COMPONENT-level Nsight Compute results (standalone benches of the same kernels at production launch configs; see ncu_status for why model-process ncu did not run). ncu durations are kernel-replay microbenchmarks (cold caches, ncu clocks), not model time; release_launch_config_in_trace gives the in-model nsys p50 of the same launch config for comparison. tensor_inst_hmma_pct_peak_active = HMMA instruction rate vs peak (a BF16 m16n8k16 HMMA keeps the pipe ~2 cycles, so ~45% means the tensor pipe is ~90% busy).
Decode attention in this build uses FlashInfer's BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheKernel (tensor-core decode path) + PersistentVariableLengthMergeStates (split-KV merge).
